```{r}

# ==== CONFIG & LIBRARIES ====

library(tidyverse)
library(caret)
library(ranger)
library(pROC)
library(glmnet)
library(xgboost)
library(Matrix)
library(yardstick)  # for macro F1
set.seed(2024)


DATA_PATH <- "/Users/ianbarbero/Downloads/Crash_Data_Cleaned_v3.csv"


# Load dataset

df <- read_csv(DATA_PATH, show_col_types = FALSE)

# Optional sampling for speed (set SAMPLE_N <- NA to use full data)

if (!exists("SAMPLE_N")) SAMPLE_N <- NA
if (!is.na(SAMPLE_N)) {
df <- df %>% sample_n(SAMPLE_N)
}

# === AUTO-DETECT TARGET COLUMN (robust) ===

# If you already know the target column name, set TARGET <- "your_column" above this file

if (!exists("TARGET")) TARGET <- "target"  # default attempt

# If default TARGET not present, try common candidate names, then fallback to a binary column auto-detect

if (!(TARGET %in% names(df))) {
candidates <- c("target","TARGET","Target","injury","Injury","severity","Severity",
"outcome","Outcome","label","Label","CrashType","crash_type","crash")
found <- intersect(candidates, names(df))
if (length(found) > 0) {
TARGET <- found[1]
message("TARGET not found as 'target' — using candidate column: ", TARGET)
} else {
# find any column with exactly 2 unique non-NA values
bin_cols <- names(df)[sapply(df, function(x) length(unique(na.omit(x))) == 2)]
if (length(bin_cols) > 0) {
TARGET <- bin_cols[1]
message("Auto-detected binary target column: ", TARGET)
} else {
# as last resort, pick a column with few unique values (<=10) and not an ID-like column
small_cols <- names(df)[sapply(df, function(x) {
ux <- unique(na.omit(x))
is.numeric(x) && length(ux) <= 10 || is.character(x) && length(ux) <= 10 || is.factor(x) && length(ux) <= 10
})]
if (length(small_cols) > 0) {
TARGET <- small_cols[1]
message("No strict binary column found; picking small-unique-values column as target: ", TARGET)
} else {
stop("Could not auto-detect a suitable target column. Please set TARGET to the correct column name.")
}
}
}
} else {
message("Using TARGET = '", TARGET, "' from config.")
}

# Print a bit of diagnostic info

cat("DATA PATH:", DATA_PATH, "\n")
cat("Detected TARGET column:", TARGET, "\n")
cat("Dataset dims:", dim(df)[1], "rows x", dim(df)[2], "cols\n")

```

```{r}

# ===== Safe train/test split with diagnostics =====

# Basic checks

if (!exists("df")) stop("Error: object 'df' not found. Load your dataset before splitting.")
if (!exists("TARGET")) stop("Error: TARGET variable not set.")

if (!(TARGET %in% names(df))) {
stop(paste0("Error: TARGET '", TARGET, "' not found in df. Available columns: ",
paste(head(names(df), 200), collapse = ", ")))
}

cat("Dataset rows:", nrow(df), " cols:", ncol(df), "\n")
if (nrow(df) < 2) stop("Error: dataset has fewer than 2 rows; cannot split.")

# Inspect target column

target_vec <- df[[TARGET]]
cat("Target column class:", class(target_vec), "\n")
na_cnt <- sum(is.na(target_vec))
cat("Target NAs:", na_cnt, "\n")

# Count unique non-NA values

unique_vals <- unique(na.omit(target_vec))
cat("Unique non-NA target values (n):", length(unique_vals), "\n")
if (length(unique_vals) == 0) stop("Error: target column contains only NA values.")

# If only one unique value, we cannot train a classifier

if (length(unique_vals) == 1) {
stop(paste0("Target has only one class: '", unique_vals, "'. Cannot train classification model."))
}

# Convert target to factor for modelling

df[[TARGET]] <- as.factor(df[[TARGET]])
cat("Target levels:", paste(levels(df[[TARGET]]), collapse = ", "), "\n")

# Choose positive class: by default choose the minority class (useful for binary classification)

tab <- table(df[[TARGET]])
pos_class <- names(sort(tab, decreasing = FALSE))[1]  # minority
cat("Positive class (chosen):", pos_class, "\n")

# Also provide the majority class just for reference

maj_class <- names(sort(tab, decreasing = TRUE))[1]
cat("Majority class:", maj_class, "\n")
POS_CLASS <- pos_class  # store for later use

# If any class has fewer than 2 observations, stratified splitting will fail; fallback to random split

if (any(tab < 2)) {
warning("At least one target class has < 2 observations; falling back to random (non-stratified) split.")
set.seed(2024)
train_idx <- sample(seq_len(nrow(df)), size = floor(0.8 * nrow(df)))
train <- df[train_idx, , drop = FALSE]
test  <- df[-train_idx, , drop = FALSE]
} else {

# Stratified split

set.seed(2024)
train_idx <- caret::createDataPartition(df[[TARGET]], p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train <- df[train_idx, , drop = FALSE]
test  <- df[-train_idx, , drop = FALSE]
}

cat("Split sizes -> train:", nrow(train), " test:", nrow(test), "\n")

# Ensure target is factor in both

train[[TARGET]] <- factor(train[[TARGET]], levels = levels(df[[TARGET]]))
test[[TARGET]]  <- factor(test[[TARGET]], levels = levels(df[[TARGET]]))
```

```{r}

# Basic preprocessing: median impute numeric, replace NA in factors with "Unknown"

numeric_cols <- names(train)[sapply(train, is.numeric)]
factor_cols  <- names(train)[sapply(train, function(x) is.character(x) || is.factor(x)) & names(train) != TARGET]

if (length(numeric_cols) > 0) {
for (col in numeric_cols) {
med <- median(train[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
train[[col]][is.na(train[[col]])] <- med
test[[col]][is.na(test[[col]])]  <- med
}
}

if (length(factor_cols) > 0) {
for (col in factor_cols) {
# convert to factor and replace NA with "Unknown"
train[[col]] <- as.character(train[[col]])
test[[col]]  <- as.character(test[[col]])
train[[col]][is.na(train[[col]])] <- "Unknown"
test[[col]][is.na(test[[col]])]  <- "Unknown"
# collapse rare levels in train (optional)
lvl_counts <- sort(table(train[[col]]), decreasing = TRUE)
# keep levels that have at least 1 observation (or change threshold)
train[[col]] <- factor(train[[col]])
test[[col]]  <- factor(test[[col]], levels = levels(train[[col]]))
}
}

# Remove ID-like columns (simple heuristic: very high cardinality and names like id)

possible_ids <- names(train)[grepl("id|ID|record", names(train), ignore.case = TRUE)]
if (length(possible_ids) > 0) {
message("Dropping possible ID columns: ", paste(possible_ids, collapse = ", "))
train <- train %>% select(-any_of(possible_ids))
test  <- test %>% select(-any_of(possible_ids))
}

# Final sanity check: ensure no infinite or NaN values

train <- train %>% mutate(across(everything(), ~ ifelse(is.infinite(.x), NA, .x)))
test  <- test  %>% mutate(across(everything(), ~ ifelse(is.infinite(.x), NA, .x)))
```

```{r}
# === RANDOM FOREST (ranger) ===


rf_model <- ranger(
formula = as.formula(paste(TARGET, "~ .")),
data = train,
num.trees = 200,
probability = TRUE,
mtry = floor(sqrt(ncol(train) - 1)),
min.node.size = 10
)

# Get probability for positive class

preds_rf <- predict(rf_model, data = test)$predictions
if (is.matrix(preds_rf) || is.data.frame(preds_rf)) {
if (POS_CLASS %in% colnames(preds_rf)) {
prob_rf <- preds_rf[, as.character(POS_CLASS)]
} else {
# fallback: pick the column corresponding to POS_CLASS by position if names absent
prob_rf <- preds_rf[, 1]
warning("Could not find POS_CLASS column in RF predictions; using first column as probability.")
}
} else {

# unexpected format

stop("Unexpected prediction format from ranger; inspect rf_model output.")
}

pred_rf <- factor(ifelse(prob_rf >= 0.5, POS_CLASS, maj_class), levels = c(maj_class, POS_CLASS))

acc_rf <- mean(pred_rf == test[[TARGET]])
mf1_rf <- yardstick::f_meas_vec(as.factor(test[[TARGET]]), pred_rf, estimator = "macro")
auc_rf <- pROC::roc(response = test[[TARGET]], predictor = prob_rf, levels = levels(test[[TARGET]]))$auc

cat(sprintf("RF -> Accuracy: %.3f | Macro-F1: %.3f | AUC: %.3f\n", acc_rf, mf1_rf, auc_rf))

```

```{r}

# Ensure packages for glmnet/xgboost are loaded (they were loaded at top, but keep safe)

add_pkgs <- c("glmnet","xgboost","Matrix")
need2 <- add_pkgs[!sapply(add_pkgs, require, character.only = TRUE)]
if (length(need2)) { try(install.packages(need2), silent = TRUE); lapply(need2, require, character.only = TRUE) }
library(glmnet); library(xgboost); library(Matrix)
set.seed(2024)
```

```{r}

# === Logistic Regression (caret::train glm) ===

set.seed(2024)
glm_fit <- caret::train(
as.formula(paste(TARGET, "~ .")),
data = train,
method = "glm",
family = "binomial",
trControl = caret::trainControl(method = "none", classProbs = TRUE)
)

glm_prob_df <- predict(glm_fit, newdata = test, type = "prob")

# pick probability column for POS_CLASS; caret returns a column per level name

if (POS_CLASS %in% names(glm_prob_df)) {
glm_probs <- glm_prob_df[[as.character(POS_CLASS)]]
} else {

# fallback: if names differ, take the second column (commonly the "positive" level)

glm_probs <- glm_prob_df[[ncol(glm_prob_df)]]
warning("POS_CLASS not found in glm prob columns; using last column as probability.")
}

glm_pred <- factor(ifelse(glm_probs >= 0.5, POS_CLASS, maj_class), levels = c(maj_class, POS_CLASS))

cm_glm <- caret::confusionMatrix(glm_pred, test[[TARGET]], positive = POS_CLASS)
auc_glm <- pROC::roc(response = test[[TARGET]], predictor = glm_probs, levels = levels(test[[TARGET]]))$auc

cat("GLM results:\n")
print(cm_glm)
cat(sprintf("GLM AUC: %.3f\n", as.numeric(auc_glm)))
```

```{r}
# === XGBoost via caret (xgbTree) ===

ctrl <- caret::trainControl(
method = "cv", number = 3,
classProbs = TRUE,
summaryFunction = twoClassSummary,
verboseIter = FALSE
)

# caret expects the positive class to be the first level of the factor passed to it when using twoClassSummary.

# To make things consistent, relevel train so that POS_CLASS is the first level and majority is second.

train_xgb <- train
train_xgb[[TARGET]] <- factor(train_xgb[[TARGET]], levels = c(POS_CLASS, setdiff(levels(train_xgb[[TARGET]]), POS_CLASS)))

test_xgb  <- test
test_xgb[[TARGET]]  <- factor(test_xgb[[TARGET]], levels = levels(train_xgb[[TARGET]]))

tune_grid <- expand.grid(
nrounds = c(50, 100),
max_depth = c(3, 6),
eta = c(0.1, 0.3),
gamma = 0,
colsample_bytree = c(0.6, 0.8),
min_child_weight = 1,
subsample = c(0.6, 0.8)
)

set.seed(2024)
xgb_fit <- caret::train(
as.formula(paste(TARGET, "~ .")),
data = train_xgb,
method = "xgbTree",
metric = "ROC",
trControl = ctrl,
tuneGrid = tune_grid
)

xgb_prob_df <- predict(xgb_fit, newdata = test_xgb, type = "prob")

# caret returns a column per level; pick the POS_CLASS column (if present) or the first column

if (POS_CLASS %in% names(xgb_prob_df)) {
xgb_probs <- xgb_prob_df[[as.character(POS_CLASS)]]
} else {
xgb_probs <- xgb_prob_df[[1]]
warning("POS_CLASS not found in xgb prob columns; using first column as probability.")
}

xgb_pred <- factor(ifelse(xgb_probs >= 0.5, POS_CLASS, maj_class), levels = c(maj_class, POS_CLASS))

cm_xgb <- caret::confusionMatrix(xgb_pred, test_xgb[[TARGET]], positive = POS_CLASS)
auc_xgb <- pROC::roc(response = test_xgb[[TARGET]], predictor = xgb_probs, levels = levels(test_xgb[[TARGET]]))$auc

cat("XGBoost bestTune:\n")
print(xgb_fit$bestTune)
cat(sprintf("XGBoost AUC: %.3f\n", as.numeric(auc_xgb)))
print(cm_xgb)

```

```{r}
# === Compare models: AUC table + ROC plot ===

results_df <- tibble::tibble(
truth = test[[TARGET]],
rf_prob  = prob_rf,
glm_prob = glm_probs,
xgb_prob = xgb_probs
)

auc_tbl <- tibble::tibble(
model = c("Random Forest", "Logistic", "XGBoost"),
AUC   = c(as.numeric(auc_rf), as.numeric(auc_glm), as.numeric(auc_xgb))
)

print(auc_tbl)

roc_rf  <- pROC::roc(results_df$truth, results_df$rf_prob)
roc_glm <- pROC::roc(results_df$truth, results_df$glm_prob)
roc_xgb <- pROC::roc(results_df$truth, results_df$xgb_prob)

plot(roc_rf, col = "black", main = "ROC Comparison")
lines(roc_glm, col = "blue")
lines(roc_xgb, col = "green")
legend("bottomright",
legend = c(
paste0("RF (AUC=", round(auc_rf,3),")"),
paste0("GLM (AUC=", round(auc_glm,3),")"),
paste0("XGB (AUC=", round(auc_xgb,3),")")
),
col = c("black","blue","green"),
lwd = 2)

```

# Confusion matrix heatmap for RF

cm_rf_table <- caret::confusionMatrix(pred_rf, test[[TARGET]], positive = POS_CLASS)$table
cm_tbl <- as.data.frame(cm_rf_table)
ggplot(cm_tbl, aes(Prediction, Reference, fill = Freq)) +

labs(title = "Confusion Matrix — Random Forest")
